title: buffer overread in fts5 (sqlite3Fts5GetVarint), reached through fts5SegIterReverse
live_proof: backport filter: upstream fix adfb203a7d removes code still present in 3.22.0, and its own regression database (decoded from the fix's hex dump) reproduces on stock 3.22.0 under host ASan as heap-use-after-free in sqlite3Fts5GetVarint
object: an fts5 leaf-page buffer held by the segment iterator
lifetime_ender: the page is released while an iterator still refers to it, then the varint decoder reads it
shape: read past the end of the record
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator: upstream's own regression image, run statement by statement through stock 3.22.0. Served from repro322_memfs.c rather than a real file -- ext/misc/memvfs.c cannot be used, it serves only the main database so the pager cannot create a rollback journal, and it takes its buffer as an integer in the URI, which on a capability machine is an untagged forged pointer

note: TITLE AND DIRECTORY NAME CORRECTED 2026-10-20. Both said use-after-free / stale read; this case's own upstream commit adfb203a7d (2021-10-01) is subject "Fix a BUFFER OVERREAD in fts5 that could occur when processing an 'ORDER BY rowid DESC' query against corrupt database records", and the fix replaces fts5DataRead with the leaf-validating fts5LeafRead in fts5SegIterReverse. The measured fault agrees: cause=28, a BOUNDS fault, not cause=25. The title is fixed here; the directory name keeps `stale_read` so that every record written against it stays resolvable, and this note is where the two disagree on purpose. Case 25 is declared a duplicate of this one: its fix 415540ddaa (2021-09-29) guards the same read two days earlier, and the two cases' pools cells are the identical fault record, {cause 28, offset 80, sqlite3Fts5GetVarint}. AXIS CORRECTED 2026-10-28, and now stated in `class` rather than left to be read out of `lifetime_ender`: this is a spatial defect. The same evidence settles it -- upstream's own subject says BUFFER OVERREAD, the fix is a leaf-validating read, `shape` is "read past the end of the record", and the measured fault is cause=28 (bounds). `lifetime_ender` still describes the released page because that is what the trigger does to reach the overread, and `tools/catch-tables.py` used to infer the axis from that sentence, which filed the case as temporal. `class` wins over the inference.
